intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that epidermolysis bullosa simplex with nephropathy and deafness (EBS7) is caused by homozygous mutation in the CD151 gene on chromosome 11p15.5.

paragraphs.text: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex with nephropathy and deafness (EBS7) combines hereditary nephritis that progresses to end-stage renal disease, pretibial epidermolysis bullosa, and sensorineural deafness. Affected individuals lack the MER2 blood group antigen, which is carried by CD151 on erythrocytes (Kagan et al., 1988; Karamatic Crew et al., 2004).

paragraphs.text: Karamatic Crew et al. (2004) showed that CD151 expresses the MER2 blood group antigen and is present on erythrocytes. They studied 3 MER2-negative patients of Indian Jewish origin with end-stage kidney disease, 2 of whom were sibs. All 3 were homozygous for a 1-bp insertion (G383) in exon 5 of the CD151 gene. The insertion causes a frameshift and a premature stop signal at codon 140. The resulting truncated protein would lack its integrin-binding domain. The authors concluded that CD151 is essential for the correct assembly of the glomerular and tubular basement membranes in the kidney, that it has functional significance in the skin, and that it is probably a component of the inner ear.

paragraphs.text: Karamatic Crew et al. (2004) studied 3 MER2-negative patients of Indian Jewish origin who had end-stage kidney disease with epidermolysis bullosa simplex with nephropathy and deafness (EBS7). Two of the patients were sibs, previously reported by Kagan et al. (1988). All 3 were homozygous for a 1-bp insertion (G383) in exon 5 of the CD151 gene. The insertion causes a frameshift and a premature stop signal at codon 140. The resulting truncated protein would lack its integrin-binding domain.
